title: Optimize / Evals 1:1 prep - 2026-03-05
content:
Goal: quick sync ahead of Friday sync - prioritize actions for the evaluation regressions and decide immediate rollbacks / canary steps.

Agenda:
- Quick status (2m) - what changed since last sync
- A/B results recap (6m) - summary of latest run (2026-03-03): metric deltas and significance
- Prompt sets & candidate regression analysis (8m)
- Hypotheses & root-cause leads (6m)
- Short-term mitigations / rollout plan (6m)
- Action items + owners (5m)

Notes / data to highlight:
- A/B summary: control -> new_prompt_v3. Compared to control, overall accept-rate dropped 3.8pp (p<0.01) on N=12k. Latency unchanged. Token cost +0.2%. Regression concentrated in the "clarity" eval slice for long-form instructions (seq_len > 512).
- Top failing prompts: prompt family 'guided-refactor' (examples 4, 9, 12). Failure mode: hallucinated variable names + missed constraints.
- Recent change that may have impacted: quantization profile updated on 2026-03-01 (int8 dynamic) + tokenizer update (v1.4) - both rolled together in the canary. We need to tease apart.

Hypotheses:
1) Tokenizer change altered tokenization boundary for common code tokens -> model sees different context window for long-form prompts. (lead: Aisha)
2) Quantization path introduced minor numeric drift amplifying hallucination on parens-heavy code. (lead: Jamie)
3) Prompt rewrite in v3 increased instruction verbosity, causing model to over-generalize on constraints. (lead: Noah)

Quick checks to run before next sync (owners + due dates):
- Run targeted eval on affected prompt family with old tokenizer + new quantization (control vs variant) to isolate tokenizer impact (Aisha) - due 2026-03-07
- Re-run eval with old quantization + new tokenizer to isolate quantization impact (Jamie) - due 2026-03-07
- Short prompt-ablation: reduce verbosity in guided-refactor prompts and run small N A/B (Noah) - due 2026-03-06
- Extract top 200 failure examples and annotate error type (false constraint vs hallucination) for triage (SWE intern) - due 2026-03-06
- Check rollout settings: pause further canaries and pin traffic to control for redirecting user-facing routes (Ops) - requested now, confirm by EOD 2026-03-05

Decision points for Friday sync:
- If tokenizer isolation shows >2pp lift when reverted, schedule tokenizer rollback for canary (actionable)
- If quantization is culprit, consider reverting to previous quant profile and re-evaluate cost delta
- If prompt verbosity is primary cause, prepare a new v3a prompt set with reduced verbosity and run canary at 10%

Open questions / ask for help:
- Can SRE provide the canary traffic split logs and per-sequence-length latency/cost breakdown for the runs on 2026-03-03? (ask @ops-team)
- Are there any other model changes rolled that week (weights patch, pos-emb tweak)? I think only quant + tokenizer + prompt, but confirm (research/ops).

Action items (concise):
- Aisha: tokenizer isolation eval (2026-03-07)
- Jamie: quantization isolation eval (2026-03-07)
- Noah: prompt-ablation + small A/B (2026-03-06)
- SWE-intern: annotate top 200 failures (2026-03-06)
- Ops: pause additional canaries + provide traffic/logs (2026-03-05 EOD)

Notes-to-self: keep the Friday sync focused on binary decisions (rollback vs keep + mitigations). Avoid long debates on minor metric noise - we only need clear actionable thresholds (e.g., >2pp drop on primary quality slice or consistent failure taxonomy).

Prep ask for meeting: bring one slide with A/B plot for clarity slice (control vs new_prompt_v3) and sample failure excerpts (annotated).

Quick links / refs:
- Eval dashboard: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/EV-221-eval-dashboard
- A/B run id: ab-run-2026-03-03-17
- Tokenizer diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer/compare/v1.3...v1.4

-- end of prep notes --
